input.summary:
P7 living room built in parts/room-49.mjs: a spruce-stair armchair group (four chairs around a fence-and-slab table) in the east half, a brown carpet rug on the lane, a barrel sideboard with a pot and candles, a chest, and four hung lanterns plus one standing on the table.
make.sh ran and wrote a whole build.nbt (21 cells placed, 0 refused, 0 off-palette). The room passes `mcd room` (walk OK, min light 9, no dark cells) only when wrapped in a test floor, ceiling and walls.
The stair column x115 z15..17 is kept clear for the joiner's flight, which is already in build.nbt; the S doorway lane (x119..120) and the N door lane are open.
left: The real floor (y1), ceiling (y5) and walls are not in this copy's shell (stub parts), so `mcd room build.nbt` reports UNREACHABLE and floating carpets and lanterns here. I verified the layout on /tmp/test56.nbt, a copy of build.nbt with a floor, ceiling and walls wrapped around the room; the real build must supply the y5 ceiling the hanging lanterns hang from.

The hearth front (124,2,17) is left empty on purpose: the focal piece is the armchair group, and the campfire outside the E wall (126,2,17) lights through the mouth (125,2,17). A hearth surround there would need the chimney part's decision.

The table is a spruce fence with a top slab at y3, so the table top sits at 4.0; the chairs are spruce stairs with backs toward the walls and the seats facing the table. A lower table would need a different form.
No plan.md checkbox covers this room alone; the 'Per house' item in elements.md is only partly met here (no kitchen stove or beds in this room).

waste.what: Wrapped the room in a test shell by hand (floor y1, ceiling y5, stone walls, two doorways) in a throwaway script, because the shared build has no shell yet and the room check reads 'no way in' and floating without it.
waste.cost: One test script, about 2 retries; the room check gave OK only after the wrap.
waste.tool: `mcd room --assume-shell` (or `mcd room --shell-box`): wrap the room box in floor, ceiling and walls from rooms.json when the neighbouring parts are still stubs, so the walk and light checks run on the room alone.

waste.what: Counted each layer row character by character to make the 10-column grid line up with x115..124 (the plan's column header was the only guide).
waste.cost: Three layers of 4 rows each, recounted about twice.
waste.tool: `layers()` could take `{ at, width }` and report a row-width mismatch; `mcd plan` could print the origin and the x index under the grid rows so the count is visible when drawing.

waste.what: Chair facings worked out by hand (stairs facing = the side of the back, so a chair looking at the table has its back to the outside).
waste.cost: Four stair facings, checked by reasoning, not by the tool.
waste.tool: A `chair(g, { x, y, z, lookAt })` helper in vocab that sets the stair facing from the seat direction, the same way bed() sets the head from facing.

companions.task: Check the light from the four hung lanterns and the table lantern against the real ceiling and the lit campfire through the E mouth once the shell is in, and say whether any floor cell drops under 8.
Decide the hearth front at (124,2,17): a brick or stone surround in front of the E mouth (125,2,17), which the chimney part has to agree on, so the focal reads as a fireplace from the door.
